abstract: Background The locus coeruleus (LC) accumulates abnormal tau early in Alzheimer's disease, yet the mechanisms linking early tauopathy to neuronal dysfunction and the potential to modify subsequent pathology remain unclear. We investigated potassium-dependent excitability control, associated molecular 5 changes and Kv7-targeted intervention. Methods We combined electrophysiology, single-cell RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry and sleep-electroencephalographic recordings in P301S tau transgenic (PS19) mice and wild-type mice receiving local LC inoculation of synthetic human tau fibrils. Pharmacological channel modulation and glycogen synthase kinase- 3 (GSK- 3) inhibition assessed pharmacological modulation of the electrophysiological phenotype. Chronic retigabine treatment assessed pathological outcomes after unilateral locus coeruleus fibril inoculation in young PS19 mice. Results Young, but not aged, PS19 mice exhibited elevated tonic firing and intrinsic excitability of locus 15 coeruleus neurons, associated with pre-tangle phosphorylated tau accumulation and reduced low-threshold potassium current density. Exploratory single-cell profiling identified candidate expression changes in marker-defined noradrenergic neurons: increased stress-associated gene expression coincided with reduced expression of neurofilament, neuronal-maintenance and potassium-channel genes, including Kcnq3 and Kcnd1. Increased nuclear RE-1 silencing 20 transcription factor (REST) and reduced Kv7.2 and Kv7.3 immunoreactivity suggested a candidate transcriptional mechanism associated with channel dysfunction. Local fibril inoculation reproduced the physiological abnormalities in wild-type mice, with hyperexcitability depending on endogenous tau. Combined Kv4/Kv7 modulation attenuated hyperexcitability, while GSK- 3; inhibition reduced tau phosphorylation, increased low-threshold potassium currents and lowered tonic firing. Both models showed increased dark-phase wakefulness and state-dependent electroencephalographic power changes. Chronic treatment with the Kv7 opener retigabine reduced bilateral LC AT8-positive tau burden and was associated with higher tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive neuronal density after unilateral seeding. Conclusions Early LC tauopathy combines impaired potassium channel-dependent excitability control with transcriptional changes consistent with cellular stress and reduced neuronal maintenance. Kv7 activation attenuates seeded tau pathology, supporting excitability regulation as a candidate intervention strategy during early tauopathy.
